multiple.scope: All reachable modeled response/error and fault choices across two sequential parts, with shared extra/protocol budgets and independent one-shot repairs. No fixed response scripts.

slots.repairOk: Accept exactly the currently anchored unresolved sourceIndex slots.

traceContract.normalization: Strip module namespaces through the last ::; reject duplicate normalized variable names.

#set: integer sourceIndex slots; normalize to sorted unique arrays

traceContract.actor: Current part number, or -1 for init/advance_time/stutter.
traceContract.phase: Durable extraction_parts.phase; not the observational stage.
traceContract.stage: idle/reserved/inflight/received/done. Successful provider responses wait at a test wrapper before the same synchronous commit-and-observer continuation.
traceContract.ready: false only when idle and awaiting the next actual persisted interval/retry/cooldown deadline; all active and terminal stages are true.
traceContract.outcome: Independent expectedOutcome specification: active stage => none; done with every phase done, every initial_complete true and every unresolved set empty => ok iff any accepted slot, else empty; all other done states => partial iff any accepted slot, else invalid. Safety compares outcome exactly and does not reuse the transition result helper.
traceContract.admit: Durable initial/repair reservation before provider dispatch. Reset current part replies to none.
traceContract.reserveFailure: One-shot reservation transaction failure; scheduler marks job partial/invalid, leaves durable part pending, and performs no new provider call.
traceContract.commitFailure: After paid successful response, storage failure is not automatically retried. Scheduler settles partial/invalid and durable part may remain inflight.
traceContract.notificationFailure: commit_notify_failure is one atomic commit+observer+settle transition, with caught notification failures. No invented asynchronous notification boundary.
traceContract.stutter: Terminal no-op over every business projection.
traceContract.cycle: One automatic cycle (1); reopening and explicit manual retry are separately identified real implementation evidence.
traceContract.clockDomain: Virtual time stays fixed during provider calls, response delivery, commit and observers; only advance_time jumps to the persisted next dispatch deadline. A slow real response already exceeding the 2000ms interval and allowing immediate continuation is outside this timing domain.

fast.tlc: Both full finite domains must finish complete enumeration.
fast.claim: Bounded Apalache only to the declared fast depths; no deep-profile claim.

deep.tlc: Same complete finite domains as fast.
deep.claim: Independent deep run; pending, interrupted, missing or timed-out checks are not passes.

profileRationale: Pre-terminalOutcome-strengthening cost probes completed depth12 at 12.91s (single) and 30.64s (two_parts), depth18 at 18.24s (single) and 224.30s (two_parts), each within a 240s process-group-cleaned bound. Fast is depth12; deep independently checks depth18. Bounds do not reduce either complete TLC finite domain; every final run must establish its own completion status.
exclusions: time elapsing during provider/commit; slow-response immediate continuation
